outcomes.text: Develop business intelligence, decision modeling, data-mining and AI skills for business decisions.

courses.name: Data Mining and AI
courses.description: Uses data mining and machine learning to identify patterns in business data and support managerial decisions.
courses.prerequisites: (VSB 2020 or SBI 3040) and VSB 2008 and (VSB 2009 :Y or SBI 3020)

courses.name: Decision Analytics & AI
courses.description: Integrates data preparation, decision modeling, programming and generative AI to solve business problems.

courses.name: Intro to Econometrics
courses.description: Uses statistical estimation, regression and forecasting to investigate economic relationships.
courses.prerequisites: (ECO 1001 or SBI 2005) and ECO 1002 and (STAT 1235 or STAT 1313 or STAT 1430 or STAT 4310 or VSB 2005)

courses.name: Applied Financial Statistics
courses.description: Applies statistical and econometric methods to financial risk, returns and other finance problems.

courses.name: Sports Analytics
courses.description: Applies R and statistical analysis to sports performance, scouting and organizational decisions.

courses.name: Database Management
courses.description: Studies relational database design, SQL, distributed databases and client-server systems.
courses.prerequisites: VSB 2006 and (VSB 2020 :Y or SBI 3040) and (VSB 2009 :Y or SBI 3020)

courses.name: CRM and Data Analytics
courses.description: Uses data warehouses, business intelligence and data mining to support organizational decisions.
courses.prerequisites: VSB 2006 and (VSB 2020 or SBI 3040) and (VSB 2009 or SBI 3020)

courses.name: Business Intelligence with AI
courses.description: Builds business-intelligence workflows with generative AI and modern data tools.
courses.prerequisites: VSB 2006 and (VSB 2020 or SBI 3040) and (VSB 2009 or SBI 3020)

courses.name: Marketing Analytics
courses.description: Applies analytical software and quantitative methods to marketing decisions.

requirements.title: Local program requirements
requirements.summary: Complete the local curriculum and applicable policies below. Published amounts are credits; credit-system normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Analytics and AI electives
requirements.summary: Choose the published number of electives, subject to the alternative and substitution policies below.

requirements.title: Unique courses
requirements.summary: Complete three unique business courses for this minor.

requirements.title: Free electives
requirements.summary: Minor courses may also satisfy free electives.

requirements.title: Joint program eligibility
requirements.summary: The following graduate-course options apply to students pursuing both Analytics and AI and the MSBAi program.

requirements.title: Graduate elective
requirements.summary: For eligible joint-program students, MSA 8105 may satisfy one Analytics and AI elective.

requirements.title: Graduate substitutions
requirements.summary: For eligible joint-program students, one additional listed substitution may count: MSA 8110 for MIS 2030; only one of that pair may count. Alternatively, MSA 8240 may replace MIS 3060; only one of that pair may count.

requirements.title: Excluded course
requirements.summary: CSC 4480 is explicitly ineligible for this minor; the co-major has a different rule.

requirements.title: Graduate permission
requirements.summary: Undergraduates need department, graduate-program and undergraduate-program permission for up to nine graduate credits. Graduate-program application requires relevant approvals. Courses must be taken while undergraduate; they cannot be applied retroactively after degree conferral.

notes: Official degree directory specifies this title for Class of 2029 and beyond, versus Business Analytics through Class of 2028. The class designation is not a launch date.
Local program inventory only; does not certify the host BBA degree. Credits are source amounts; credit-unit normalization is unverified. Pool subtotals are not required totals.

Required-course descriptions are original summaries of separate course catalog entries; prerequisites preserve source notation (:Y is not interpreted). Their sources are registered separately while course source_id remains the program catalog.
Conditional graduate substitutes are not ordinary unrestricted electives. Remaining unverified elective metadata and public syllabi remain null as detailed in the audit.

Eight undergraduate elective catalog records were reviewed. MGT 3180 has an AI title but its description discusses generic management, motivation, leadership and culture; its description remains unknown rather than supplying inferred AI content. Its published junior/senior restriction and prerequisite are retained. MKT 2240 says "Maximum of 5 VSB minors" without explaining the scope; this is not translated into a limit on how many minors a student can declare. The three conditional graduate MSA options still require the existing approvals; their individual course metadata remains unverified. These descriptive gaps do not change the explicit local choice and approval rules. Published credits remain unnormalized.
